findings.problem: fs::read_to_string(path).unwrap() panics on any I/O error (missing file, permission denied, etc.)
findings.failure_mode: untrusted file path causes thread panic instead of returning a typed I/O or ParseError
findings.fix: Return Result<Vec<Record>, MetricError> and use fs::read_to_string(path).map_err(|e| MetricError::Io(e)) or equivalent fallible path

findings.problem: parts[1].parse::<u32>().unwrap() panics on non-numeric value in the second CSV field
findings.failure_mode: malformed CSV line (e.g. value=abc) aborts the entire metric load instead of returning Invalid/Parse error
findings.fix: Use .parse::<u32>().map_err(|_| MetricError::Invalid) and propagate via Result

findings.problem: Lossy narrowing cast: .unwrap() as u16 silently truncates values > 65535
findings.failure_mode: A valid u32 value like 70000 wraps to 4448 in the Record, producing incorrect metrics with no error signal
findings.fix: Use u16::try_from(parsed_u32).map_err(|_| MetricError::Invalid) to reject out-of-range values

findings.problem: Unchecked indexing: parts[0] and parts[1] access Vec elements without bounds check
findings.failure_mode: A CSV line with fewer than 2 comma-separated fields (e.g. "foo" or empty string) causes panic via IndexOfBounds
findings.fix: Use split_once(',') and .ok_or(MetricError::Invalid) to get exactly two fields, or use get(0)/get(1) with .ok_or()

findings.problem: println!() call inside load_metrics - I/O side effect in a function that should be a pure parsing core
findings.failure_mode: Hidden logging side effect corrupts stdout, makes the function non-deterministic in output, and prevents headless/benchmark usage
findings.fix: Remove println! entirely from the core parse path. If logging is needed, push it to an explicit shell wrapper that calls the pure core

findings.problem: load_metrics mixes I/O (fs::read_to_string) with parsing logic in a single function
findings.failure_mode: Cannot unit-test the parsing logic without real files; cannot swap in mock I/O; violates pure-core separation
findings.fix: Split into a pure fn parse_records(text: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, MetricError> and a shell fn load_metrics(path: &str) -> Result<Vec<Record>, MetricError> that reads and delegates

findings.problem: Record uses raw String and u16 with no domain invariants encoded in the type
findings.failure_mode: A Record can be constructed with an empty name or invalid value; no typestate or smart constructor enforces domain rules
findings.fix: Add a newtype Name(String) with a constructor that validates non-empty, and use a fallible constructor for Record: impl Record { fn new(name: Name, value: u16) -> Self { ... } } or return Result

findings.problem: Collects all split parts into Vec<String> with intermediate allocations for each line
findings.failure_mode: Unnecessary heap allocations per line; for a CSV with only 2 fields, split_once + &str slices would avoid all per-line heap allocation
findings.fix: Use line.split_once(',').ok_or(...)? then work with &str slices directly; only allocate the final Record fields

findings.problem: No benchmark exists for load_metrics. The function performs I/O and parsing; any performance claim is unsupported
findings.failure_mode: Cannot verify whether this implementation meets latency/throughput requirements for metric loading workloads
findings.fix: Add a criterion or minitrace benchmark with a realistic CSV workload, baseline the current implementation, and measure any changes

findings.problem: No profiler evidence (flamegraph, perf, or similar) for the allocation profile of load_metrics
findings.failure_mode: Unknown whether intermediate Vec<String> allocations per line create measurable GC pressure or allocation overhead at scale
findings.fix: Run with cargo-flamegraph or perf record to measure allocation hotspots in the parse path

findings.problem: No try_reserve or capacity planning before Vec growth in the intermediate parts collection
findings.failure_mode: Each line's Vec<String> reallocates as parts grow; for lines with many fields this causes O(log n) reallocations
findings.fix: If collecting into Vec is retained, call try_reserve or estimate field count; prefer split_once to avoid Vec entirely

findings.problem: No benchmark, profiler, or allocation measurement evidence exists for this crate
findings.failure_mode: Performance claims about load_metrics are unsubstantiated; no baseline exists for regression testing
findings.fix: Add a workload-specific benchmark (criterion or similar), capture profiler data, and record allocation counts with #[global_allocator] tracking or dhat-rs

missing_evidence: no benchmark exists for load_metrics or any performance claim
no profiler data (flamegraph, perf, or equivalent) for the parse path
no allocation tracking (dhat-rs, jemalloc, or similar) for Vec growth in parsing
no second-ring evidence: no integration test exercising real file I/O paths (missing file, permission denied, malformed CSV)
no command evidence: cargo test, cargo fmt, or cargo clippy were not executed
residual_risk: Static review only with no commands run. The crate has multiple BLOCKER violations: four unwrap() calls (I/O panic, parse panic, bounds panic, cast panic), hidden println! I/O side effect in core logic, no functional core/shell separation, raw types without domain invariants, and zero performance evidence. A compliant fix would introduce a typed error enum, split I/O from parsing, use split_once + try_from for field extraction, remove all println! and unwrap(), and add benchmarks. Residual risk is high until these are fixed and verified.
